note: CEILINGS, not a measured baseline. These are budgets a healthy run must stay under, chosen with ~5x headroom over observed healthy numbers so machine drift, a cold runner or a noisy neighbor can never fire them — and so they never need re-blessing per machine. Breaching one means an ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE regression, not jitter. See engineering/decisions/2026-08-03-performance-guard.md.

observed.note: What a healthy tree measured when these ceilings were set (2026-08-03, headless Chromium, 4x CPU throttle, 40-slide decks). Recorded for context only — nothing compares against these, so they never go stale in a way that breaks a gate.

regressionScale.note: The regression these exist to catch, for scale. Before #1280 the gallery deck re-parsed the WHOLE deck on every keystroke because the progress rail and watermark glyph derived their section by walking every section.

emulator.note: NO SEPARATE HARNESS, and this is a finding rather than an omission. lattice-emulator.js:1673 calls latticeEngine.createEngine() and :1683 calls engine.render() — the P2 swap (2026-06-11-emulator-on-engine-p2.md) left it a wrapper with no render path of its own. `bench`'s render tier already times exactly the code it runs, and `bench --export` times the PDF/rasterize tier it adds on top. Building an emulator bench would measure the same code twice and then need re-blessing twice.
